key: # The life of each officer of the scenario, keyed by officer.<key> (docs/EUROPE.md, E4).
# Written by misc/make_tier_officers.py from the column life of source/officers.tsv. The pack wrote each life in its own words.

text: A warlord from Pei. In 196 he brought Emperor Xian to Xu and started military farms. He later ruled the north and his son founded Wei.
A cousin of Cao Cao. An arrow took his eye in 198, and he fought on. He held the rear and built dams for the farms.
A cousin of Cao Cao, famous for fast marches. He ruled the west for Cao Cao and fell at Mount Dingjun.
A cousin of Cao Cao. He held Jiangling against Zhou Yu and Fancheng against Guan Yu.
A cousin of Cao Cao. At Xingyang in 190 he gave his horse to Cao Cao and saved his life. He was very rich.
A younger brother of Cao Ren. He led the elite cavalry of Cao Cao and took the head of Yuan Tan.
A scholar of Yingchuan. He kept the capital and the supplies for Cao Cao and sent him many able men.
A nephew of Xun Yu. He joined Cao Cao in 196 and gave the plans that beat Lü Bu and Yuan Shao.
A young adviser from Yingchuan. He read the minds of the rivals of Cao Cao. He died on the return from the Wuhuan war.
An officer of Dong commandery. He held three counties for Cao Cao when Lü Bu took Yan province in 194.
The bodyguard of Cao Cao, a man of great strength. He died at the gate of the camp at Wancheng in 197.
A strong man of Qiao. He led a band of local men to Cao Cao and became his guard.
A general known for strict discipline. He surrendered to Guan Yu at the flood of Fancheng in 219.
A short and brave officer. He was often the first man on the walls.
A young officer who liked books. He moved his clan of more than ten thousand people to Ye.
An honest official. He told Cao Cao to serve the emperor and to farm the land.
An official who made the plan to move Emperor Xian from Luoyang to Xu in 196.
A strict magistrate. He later built the new city of Hefei against Wu.
An officer of Yang Feng. He joined Cao Cao at the end of 196 and later broke the siege of Fancheng.
The head of the Yuan clan, the strongest lord of the north. Cao Cao beat him at Guandu in 200.
The eldest son of Yuan Shao. In 196 he took Beihai from Kong Rong.
The second son of Yuan Shao. He later governed You province.
The favourite son of Yuan Shao. His war with Yuan Tan opened the north to Cao Cao.
A famous general of Yuan Shao. Guan Yu killed him at Baima in 200.
A cavalry general of Yuan Shao. He died at Yanjin in 200.
An adviser who spoke the truth to Yuan Shao. Yuan Shao put him in prison and then killed him.
An adviser who told Yuan Shao to take the emperor first. Cao Cao captured him at Guandu.
An official of Yuan Shao. He held Ye against Cao Cao for months in 204.
An adviser of Yuan Shao from Nanyang. He helped Yuan Shao to take Ji province.
An old friend of Cao Cao. At Guandu he left Yuan Shao and told Cao Cao where the grain was.
An adviser of Yuan Shao who later served Yuan Tan.
A general of Yuan Shao. He joined Cao Cao at Guandu and served Wei for thirty years.
A general of Yuan Shao who went to Cao Cao with Zhang He.
An officer from Liang province. His crossbowmen beat the White Horse cavalry of Gongsun Zan at Jieqiao.
An old colonel of the capital. He guarded the grain of Yuan Shao at Wuchao.
An adviser of Yuan Shao who went with Yuan Tan.
A younger brother of Xin Ping. He later served Wei and spoke boldly to its emperors.
A nephew of Yuan Shao. He later governed Bing province.
A lord of You province. His White Horse Volunteers fought the Wuhuan. He died in his tower at Yijing.
The son of Gongsun Zan. He went to the Heishan army for help in 199.
The governor of Qing province for Gongsun Zan. Yuan Tan drove him out.
An adviser of Gongsun Zan. He died in the battle of Yijing.
The governor of Liaodong. He ruled the northeast as a king and fought Goguryeo.
The son of Gongsun Du. He sent the heads of Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi to Cao Cao.
An officer of Gongsun Du in Liaodong.
An officer of Gongsun Du in Liaodong.
A warrior from Wuyuan, called the Flying General. In 196 he took Xu province from Liu Bei.
An adviser who turned against Cao Cao in 194 and gave Yan province to Lü Bu.
An officer of Lü Bu who later served Cao Cao. At Hefei in 215 he beat a large army of Wu.
An honest officer of Lü Bu. His small elite unit broke many lines of the enemy.
A leader of the bands of Taishan who joined Lü Bu and later Cao Cao.
A relative of Lü Bu who gave Chen Gong to Cao Cao in 199.
An officer of Lü Bu who surrendered at Xiapi.
An officer of Lü Bu who surrendered at Xiapi.
A local noble of Xu province. He served Lü Bu but helped Cao Cao. He governed Guangling well.
The father of Chen Deng. His words broke the alliance of Lü Bu and Yuan Shu.
A man of the Han clan from Zhuo. In 196 Lü Bu took Xiapi from him, and he moved to Xiaopei. He later founded Shu.
A sworn brother of Liu Bei from Hedong. He killed Yan Liang at Baima and later held Jing province.
A sworn brother of Liu Bei. At the bridge of Changban he stopped the army of Cao Cao with a shout.
An old friend of Liu Bei from Zhuo. He was a good envoy.
A rich merchant of Donghai. He gave his money and his sister to Liu Bei in 196.
A scholar of Beihai. He was an envoy of Liu Bei to Yuan Shao and to Liu Biao.
A younger brother of Mi Zhu. In 219 he gave Jiangling to Wu.
A cousin of Yuan Shao who ruled Huainan. He named himself emperor in 197.
A general of Yuan Shu. In 196 Lü Bu shot an arrow into a halberd and stopped his attack on Liu Bei.
A general of Yuan Shu.
A general of Yuan Shu. Cao Cao killed him in 197.
An official of Yuan Shu who spoke against the claim of an emperor.
The chief clerk of Yuan Shu.
An officer of Yuan Shu who later became a bandit chief.
An officer of Yuan Shu who later became a bandit chief.
The governor of Lujiang for Yuan Shu. Sun Ce took his city in 199.
A former White Wave leader who guarded the emperor on the road to Luoyang. He went to Yuan Shu at the end of 196.
A former White Wave leader who guarded the emperor with Yang Feng.
The son of Sun Jian, called the Little Conqueror. From 194 to 199 he took the lands south of the Yangtze.
The younger brother of Sun Ce. He was a good judge of men. He later founded Wu.
A cousin of Sun Ce who governed Yuzhang for him.
The uncle of Sun Ce, the governor of Danyang.
A friend of Sun Ce from Lujiang. He led the fleet that burned the ships of Cao Cao at Red Cliffs.
A scholar from Pengcheng. Sun Ce gave him the government of his lands.
A scholar and writer from Guangling. He was an envoy of Sun Ce to the court.
An old officer of Sun Jian. He shared the command with Zhou Yu at Red Cliffs.
An old officer of Sun Jian. At Red Cliffs his false surrender sent fire ships into the fleet of Cao Cao.
An old officer of Sun Jian, good with the bow on a horse.
An early follower of Sun Ce. He kept the accounts with a strict hand.
An old officer of Sun Jian. He governed Wu commandery for many years.
An early follower of Sun Ce from Jiujiang.
An early follower of Sun Ce. In 196 he saved Sun Quan from bandits at Xuancheng with twelve wounds.
An archer of Donglai. He fought Sun Ce in a duel at Shenting and then joined him.
An officer of Sun Ce from Lujiang. He led the guard units.
A young officer who later studied hard. In 219 his men dressed as merchants and took Jing province.
The governor of Kuaiji, a scholar of the classics. Sun Ce beat him in 196, and he later served Wei.
A scholar of Kuaiji and a master of the Book of Changes. He later served Sun Ce.
The leader of a strong band in Wu commandery. Sun Ce beat him.
The inspector of Yang province for the court. Sun Ce drove him to Yuzhang, and he died there in 197.
The governor of Yuzhang, an honest official. He later served Wei as a high minister.
An officer of Liu Yao.
A scholar of the Han clan, the governor of Jing province. He kept peace there and opened schools.
The eldest son of Liu Biao. He was a friend of Liu Bei.
An adviser of Liu Biao. He told Liu Biao to rule with benevolence.
An adviser of Liu Biao. He called the chiefs of the bandits to a feast and killed them.
A noble of Xiangyang and the brother-in-law of Liu Biao. He led the fleet of Jing province.
The governor of Jiangxia. His men shot Sun Jian. Sun Quan killed him in 208.
The governor of Changsha. He rose against Liu Biao in 198.
A general of Liu Biao. He held Jiangxia for Wei for decades.
A nephew of Liu Biao. He often fought Sun Ce in Changsha.
An officer in Changsha. At an old age he killed Xiahou Yuan at Mount Dingjun.
An adviser of Liu Biao. He went to the court at Xu and praised Cao Cao.
An official from Shanyang in Jing province. He later served Liu Bei as an envoy.
The nephew of Zhang Ji. In 196 he took the army of his uncle and held Wancheng.
An adviser from Wuwei. His plans beat Cao Cao at Wancheng twice. He later served Wei.
A strong officer of Zhang Xiu.
The governor of Yi province after his father Liu Yan. He gave Yi province to Liu Bei in 214.
A high officer of Liu Zhang. He rose against him in 200.
An official of Liu Zhang who later served Liu Bei and Wei.
An official of Liu Zhang. He hung himself from the city gate to warn Liu Zhang.
An official of Liu Zhang with a strong memory. He gave the maps of Yi province to Liu Bei.
An adviser from Fufeng who came to Yi province in 196. He later planned the war of Hanzhong for Liu Bei.
An officer from Fufeng who came with Fa Zheng. He changed sides three times.
A general of Liu Zhang. He died loyal at Luo.
The governor of Ba commandery. He told Zhang Fei that Ba had only generals who lost their heads.
An old friend of the family of Liu Zhang. He governed Baxi.
An officer who came to Yi province with Liu Yan. He later led the armies of Shu.
An adviser of Liu Zhang. He told Liu Zhang to burn the fields before Liu Bei.
The master of the Way of the Five Pecks of Rice. He ruled Hanzhong as a church state for thirty years.
The younger brother of Zhang Lu. He held the pass of Yangping against Cao Cao in 215.
An adviser of Zhang Lu. He told him not to take the title of king.
A general of Zhang Lu.
A general of Zhang Lu.
An adviser of Zhang Lu who took bribes.
A general of Dong Zhuo. He took Chang'an in 192 and held the court until 195.
A general of Dong Zhuo and the partner of Li Jue. The two men fought each other in Chang'an.
A nephew of Li Jue.
A general of Liang province with a Qiang mother. He shared the west with Han Sui.
The eldest son of Ma Teng. In 211 he led the armies of the west against Cao Cao at Tong Pass.
A son of Ma Teng.
A son of Ma Teng.
An officer of Ma Teng. At Fancheng in 219 he died before he surrendered.
A leader of the Liang rebels for thirty years. He fought Cao Cao at Tong Pass in 211.
The loyal adviser of Han Sui.
A strong officer of Han Sui. He almost killed Ma Chao with a spear.
The governor of Henei. He gave food to the emperor on the road to Luoyang in 196.
An officer of Zhang Yang who killed him in 198.
An officer of Zhang Yang who killed Yang Chou.
The leader of the Heishan army in the Taihang mountains. People called him the Flying Swallow for his speed.
A chief of the Heishan army.
A chief of the Heishan army.
The governor of Jiaozhi for forty years. He kept the far south in peace and favoured learning.
A younger brother of Shi Xie.
A younger brother of Shi Xie, the governor of Nanhai.
An officer from Changshan. He left Gongsun Zan and joined Liu Bei in 200. At Changban he saved the son of Liu Bei.
A rich man of Linhuai. He gave half of his grain to Zhou Yu and later planned the alliance with Liu Bei.
A river pirate from Ba. He later served Wu and raided the camp of Cao Cao with one hundred men.
A scholar of Yingchuan in Jing province. He told Liu Bei about Zhuge Liang.
A young scholar who moved to Jing province. He later governed Shu and made new machines for its army.
A scholar of Xiangyang, known as the Young Phoenix. He judged men well. He died at Luo.
An officer of Yiyang. He later held Hanzhong for Shu for many years.
A noble of Henei. He served Cao Cao from 208 and later held the power of Wei.
A noble of Wu commandery. In 222 he burned the camps of Liu Bei at Yiling.
The daughter of Cai Yong, a poet and musician. The Xiongnu took her north. Cao Cao paid a ransom for her in 207.
A general of Dong Zhuo at Huayin. He helped the officials of the court on the road east.
